facts: Savitribai and other members of her family were sitting in the courtyard of the former's house at about 4 p.m. on 2.3.1991.
Prahladsingh, Ambaram, Patiram, Hukum, Narayan and Girdhari were drinking liquor.
Savitribai came out from her house and asked them to behave themselves.
They started assaulting her, causing injuries inter alia by throwing stones.
When Accused Hukum hurled a stone at her, Prem Singh, brother of Savitribai intervened.
Hukum pelted a stone at him causing injury on his head.
Ambaram, who was carrying an axe, inflicted a blow on his head from its blunt side.
Other accused persons entered her house.
Patiram brought a bow and arrow and shot an arrow at Premsingh.
One Chandrakalabai pulled out that arrow.
Others who were returning from the weekly market intervened.
At least six of them namely Himmatsingh, Gendalal, Mansingh, Kamalasingh, Savitribai and Phool Singh were injured by the appellants.
issues: Whether the appellant's actions constituted murder or culpable homicide
Whether the prosecution had established that the appellant had committed the offence with common intention
petitioner_arguments: The appellant only inflicted a blow on Prem Singh's head from the blunt side of an axe, which did not cause vital injury.
Only one injury was inflicted by the appellant.
respondent_arguments: The appellants were armed with various lethal weapons and caused death to one person and injuries to six others.
The injuries found on the deceased's body support the prosecution case.
court_reasoning: The court held that the appellant had actively associated himself in the entire episode and had assaulted Prem Singh with an axe, causing injury.
The court noted that the number of injuries is not decisive; how and in what manner injuries have been caused would be a relevant factor.

The court distinguished between clause (b) of Section 299 and clause (3) of Section 300, noting that the distinction lies between a bodily injury likely to cause death and a bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
